entities.summary: María Zambrano Alarcón was a Spanish philosopher, intellectual and essayist. Her extensive work between poetic reflection and civic engagement started to be recognized in Spain over the last quarter of the 20th century after living many years in exile. She was awarded the Prince of Asturias Award (1981) and in 1989 became the first woman to receive the Miguel de Cervantes Prize (1988), the highest literary honor in the Spanish-speaking world. Spanish scholarship often places Zambrano in the company of twentieth-century women such as Simone Weil, Hannah Arendt, and her close friend and contemporary Rosa Chacel.
